title: Early Return
concept: You can use return inside an if to exit a function early when certain conditions are met.
why: Early returns handle edge cases up front, keeping the main logic clean and avoiding deeply nested code.
tips: Early returns handle 'edge cases' at the top — the happy path flows straight through
Each `return` is an exit door — the function stops there
Guard clauses check preconditions: 'is this valid?' before doing work
Early returns reduce nesting and make code more readable
common_mistakes: Having code after a return in the same branch — it's dead code
Forgetting that every path must return a value of the right type
Overusing early returns for minor checks — one or two guards is plenty
